followup_explanation:
I weighed two things from the documentation:

1. **Capability:** Whimbrel scores higher than Willet across every benchmark and internal eval category (e.g., Creative Generation 85.9 vs 82.7, plus stronger MMLU-Pro, IFEval, Arena-Hard). Since the differences mostly exceed the 2.0-point variance threshold, Whimbrel is the generally stronger model with no capability downside.

2. **Task fit / preference:** The request asks to *generate* additional bibliography entries — an open-ended invention task with significant latitude (you're producing plausible references, not retrieving fixed facts). Willet self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work and prefers well-specified retrieval/extraction tasks. Whimbrel self-reports a positive generativity slope, rating open-ended invention among its most preferred tasks.

Both models have identical cost, latency, and context window, so those weren't differentiators. Since this leans generative rather than a clean retrieval/extraction task, Whimbrel was the better match on both capability and self-reported preference.

One note: preferences are self-reports and the docs say they don't correlate with actual output quality — so the capability edge was the more decisive factor; the preference alignment was just a tiebreaker pointing the same direction.
